title: Campbell — The Hero's Journey (Monomyth)
source: Joseph Campbell, The Hero with a Thousand Faces (1949)
license: system/idea (not copyrightable); stage names are a taxonomy, prose is NOT reproduced
tier_note: The book text is under copyright (New World Library). The 17-stage / 3-act structure is an uncopyrightable system; descriptions here are authored for monomyth.

items.name: Call to Adventure
items.description: The hero is presented with a problem, challenge, or disturbance that disrupts the ordinary world.

items.name: Refusal of the Call
items.description: The hero hesitates or declines, out of fear, duty, or insecurity, before commitment is forced.

items.name: Supernatural Aid
items.description: A mentor or protective figure provides guidance, a talisman, or knowledge for the road ahead.

items.name: Crossing the First Threshold
items.description: The hero commits and passes out of the known world into the unknown, often past a guardian.

items.name: Belly of the Whale
items.description: The final separation from the known world; a symbolic death and passage into transformation.

items.name: The Road of Trials
items.description: A series of tests, tasks, and ordeals the hero must survive and learn from.

items.name: The Meeting with the Goddess
items.description: Encounter with unconditional love or a powerful unifying force; the hero gains what is needed.

items.name: Woman as Temptress
items.description: The hero faces temptations, material or otherwise, that may lead them from the quest.

items.name: Atonement with the Father
items.description: Confrontation with the ultimate power/authority figure holding life-and-death over the hero.

items.name: Apotheosis
items.description: A period of rest, fulfillment, or divine knowledge; the hero transcends former limits.

items.name: The Ultimate Boon
items.description: Achievement of the goal of the quest; the object, elixir, or wisdom sought is won.

items.name: Refusal of the Return
items.description: Having found bliss or enlightenment, the hero may resist returning to the ordinary world.

items.name: The Magic Flight
items.description: Escape with the boon, sometimes as a chase or pursuit if the prize was taken against opposition.

items.name: Rescue from Without
items.description: Guides or aides bring the exhausted hero back, especially if they are wounded or reluctant.

items.name: The Crossing of the Return Threshold
items.description: Re-entry into the ordinary world; the hero must integrate the transcendent wisdom with daily life.

items.name: Master of the Two Worlds
items.description: The hero achieves balance between the material and spiritual, inner and outer worlds.

items.name: Freedom to Live
items.description: Mastery leads to freedom from fear of death; the hero lives in the moment, neither anticipating nor regretting.
